wi_woods_the.blurb: A wooded corner of the Westby boulders in west-central Wisconsin, where scattered sandstone blocks and low ridges sit among the trees. All 14 problems are bouldering, and the spread is friendly: most fall between V0 and V2, with a handful at V3 and V4 and a single V6 at the top end. Reaching them means following woodland trails past the park restrooms, with a lower trail serving some problems and an upper trail the rest. Sandstone here tends toward slopey holds, and moss and lichen come back fast, so lightly climbed blocks can be dirty.

wi_05_condor_corner.blurb: A quiet, out-of-the-way wall on the east bluff above Devil's Lake in the Baraboo Range, standing somewhat taller than the crags around it. It holds 14 routes, almost all of them traditional with one top-rope line. Grades are gentle to middling: mostly 5.4 to 5.9, with a few harder pitches reaching into the 5.10s and one top-rope test at 5.11. Bring a trad rack. Approaching from the neighbouring Aladdin's Castle, you traverse east at the same level and drop down a little to get around a corner before the main face comes into view.

wi_10_moldy_buttress.blurb: A small, lesser-visited formation on the East Rampart at Devil's Lake, sitting between its two neighbouring buttresses. The 14 routes are single pitch, mostly 40 to 50 feet, split between trad leads and top-rope lines. Grades start at 5.2 and run to 5.12, though the bulk sit around 5.8, so it suits climbers working through moderate cracks and faces. The rock is quartzite and gets slick when wet; spring and fall bring good friction, while leafy summer cover provides shade. Anchors are sparse, so a rack leaning toward small cams and nuts is the norm.
wi_10_moldy_buttress.approach: From the CCC trail, turn left at the Pedestal Buttress junction and follow the climbers' trail roughly 300 feet west.

wi_hidden_buttress.blurb: A peaceful buttress at Devil's Lake, set closer to the road than Stettner's Rocks and often used as a warm-up before harder climbing at White Wall. It has 14 routes, mostly trad and top-rope, with a spread from about 5.5 up through the low 5.11s. The middle of the range is well served, with several lines in the 5.8 to 5.10 band. Expect a short scramble through trees to reach the first solid rock.

wi_d_arcy_s_buttress.blurb: One of the busiest short walls on the East Rampart at Devil's Lake, around 40 feet tall and popular for its varied routes and quick access. Most of the 14 lines are trad, with some top-rope climbs and a boulder problem on the north side. Grades are broad: easy 5.3 and 5.4 lines, a good run of 5.6 to 5.10 climbs, and a single 5.13 for the strongest. On summer weekends the base can be crowded by mid-morning, so arrive early. From the CCC trail, take a left at The Monster, then go right at Pedestal Buttress for a short stroll.

wi_6_porkchop_buttress.blurb: A tall piece of rock on the south end of Devil's Lake's West Bluff, grouped with The Pantry, Dungeon Wall and Split Tower below Misery Rocks. The wooded setting keeps it shaded and secluded in summer. It carries 14 climbs, mostly traditional leads with a few top-rope lines and a couple of boulder problems at the base. Trad grades run from 5.5 to 5.8 for the bulk, with a pair of harder top-ropes around 5.11, and boulder problems at V1 and V2. It can be reached from above by going down north of the Frigate formation, and at least one serious accident has happened here.

wi_aberdeen_quarry_north.blurb: The larger of two bouldering sections in an old granite quarry beside Dave's Falls County Park in the Northern Highlands of Wisconsin, holding the densest cluster of boulders in the park. All 14 problems are bouldering, running from about V1 up to V7 with the weight in the middle: V2 through V5 make up most of the list, and a few harder problems finish it off. A number of lines only come into condition in winter when the water freezes. Walk the park trail past the river bridge, then follow the social trail to the railway tracks; the boulders are just beyond.
